reason: No prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises. The hypothesis relies on specific claims about Zr-induced lattice distortion, Ni7Zr2 precipitate formation, their effects on dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding, the role of ZrO2 in passive film stability, and the trade-off at x = 0.1, but none of these are supported by referenced passages. The baseline properties are also stated without citation.
premises: Zr addition causes lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening in the FCC/B2 matrix
At x ≥ 0.05, Zr forms fine, coherent/semi-coherent Ni7Zr2 precipitates that impede dislocations and grain-boundary sliding
Ni7Zr2 precipitates and microstructural refinement improve corrosion resistance by forming a stable ZrO2-containing passive film
Excess Zr (x = 0.1) coarsens precipitates, degrading mechanical properties while possibly improving corrosion resistance
The baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has specific mechanical and corrosion properties (yield strength ~705 MPa, Icorr ~0.09993 μA/cm², etc.)
